clue.text: Extra lavish meal is customary

parts.note: a wide is a cricket extra, a run awarded for a ball bowled out of the batter's reach
a spread is a generous feast laid out on the table

explanation.surface: A lavish banquet as an extra is the usual thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A WIDE is one of cricket's 'extras', runs given away by the bowling side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common or prevalent everywhere is customary, the general practice.

clue.text: Silly walk makes wife go off

parts.note: to addle is to go rotten, as an egg goes off

explanation.surface: A man's silly walk drives his wife to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A waddle is a comical, duck-like rolling gait, a silly sort of walk.

clue.text: Request to confess providing drugs

parts.note: 'do' as in 'do come' makes a polite request
to sing is underworld slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: A detective's plea for a confession comes with an offer of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces read 'do sing!', an urging to confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosing someone means administering medicine, giving them drugs.

clue.text: Farmer has accident under blade of plough

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece placed under another follows it

parts.note: a share, or ploughshare, is the cutting blade of a plough
to come a cropper is to have a fall or accident

explanation.surface: A farmer is hurt when the plough's blade goes over him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is a British idiom for a heavy fall or mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharecropper is a tenant farmer who pays rent with a share of the crop.

clue.text: Bar bird

definitions.meaning: a ... is a bar, as a towel ... or a handrail
the ... is a wading marsh bird, like the water ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both a horizontal rod and a family of marsh birds share this one name.

clue.text: Charge a liberal group of diplomats

parts.note: a legation is a diplomatic mission headed by a minister

explanation.surface: A Liberal embassy delegation is accused of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegation is an accusation, a charge made against someone.

clue.text: Fight Pole

definitions.meaning: a pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Boxing practice and a ship's pole are the two senses of this short word.

clue.text: Guerrilla fighter aspirant to revolt

indicators.note: letters that revolt rise up and overturn their order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aspiring guerrilla wants to lead an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an armed resistance group fighting occupiers.

clue.text: Judge again makes notes about fools

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, here the notes surrounding the fools

parts.note: re is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale (do, re, mi), so res are notes
asses are idiots, fools

explanation.surface: An examiner jots down notes about idiots before judging them again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate or appraise something a second time.

clue.text: Good-looking girl fit to seduce the Italian with scanty clothing

parts.note: dish is dated slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: fit seducing the Italian draws him in, so these letters take the other piece inside

parts.note: able means fit, capable
il is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: A pretty girl in skimpy clothes sets out to seduce an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishabille is a state of being only partly or casually dressed.

clue.text: Song beginning missed by girl in West Side Story

indicators.note: the girl's name loses its first letter, so her opening is dropped

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story

explanation.surface: A singer misses the start of a number in West Side Story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maria' is itself a song from West Side Story, which adds to the musical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song, typically in an opera.

clue.text: Try becoming popular on social media — it's agonising

parts.note: a court will hear a case, that is try it
a topic trending is gaining sudden popularity online

explanation.surface: Chasing online popularity turns out to be painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-rending describes something causing deep grief or distress.

clue.text: In Berlin Germans hang around

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Germans in Berlin are loitering.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on, loiter or dawdle somewhere.

clue.text: Somehow liaises engaging good Spanish singer

indicators.note: engaging means taking on or holding, so one piece goes inside the other
somehow suggests the letters arrive in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone liaises with a good Spanish singer in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' scrambles LIAISES, and 'engaging' sets G inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Julio Iglesias, and his son Enrique, are famous singers from Spain.

clue.text: Breaking resistance getting into trendy group

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: getting into shows the resistance goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a faction is a group within a larger body
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Resistance fighters get into a fashionable clique.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a breach of a rule, a breaking of the law.

clue.text: Some Christians surreally portrayed by artist in rain

indicators.note: something portrayed surreally is distorted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Churchgoers are shown in a dreamlike painting by an artist out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinitarians are Christians who believe in the Trinity of Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

clue.text: One of S Coe's rivals breathed heavily not finishing disorderly race

parts.note: Steve Cram, written S Cram like S Coe, was a British middle-distance rival of Sebastian Coe

indicators.note: not finishing means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: blew means puffed, breathed hard

explanation.surface: A rival of Seb Coe, gasping for breath, fails to finish a chaotic race.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram and Seb Coe were British running stars of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a hurried, disorderly rush or struggle.

clue.text: Person died — search thoroughly for poisonous plant

parts.note: a man is a person
to rake through something is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone died, and a thorough search turns up a poisonous plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a toxic plant of the nightshade family, famous for its forked root.

clue.text: Round of applause for every managing body giving signal for action

parts.note: a clap is a burst of applause
per means for each
a board of directors manages a company

explanation.surface: Directors are applauded at every meeting before giving the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'Action!', the director's call when filming starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapperboard is snapped shut in front of the camera as filming of a take begins.

clue.text: One's carried part of song

definitions.meaning: a load is what someone has to carry
the ... of a song is its refrain or chorus

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy load and a song's recurring refrain are both called by this word.

clue.text: Sudden gust in full pelt round lake

indicators.note: round means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an animal in full pelt has a thick coat of fur, so is furry

explanation.surface: A gust blows round a lake at full speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In full pelt' looks like 'at full speed' but means 'covered in fur'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flurry is a brief gust of wind or swirl of snow.

clue.text: Those hearing poet keeping one in church

parts.note: W H Auden was an English poet
I is the Roman numeral for one
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A poet stays in church while one attends.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is the group of people listening to a performance.

clue.text: Book regularly produced answer in reverse

indicators.note: in shows the answer letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: to annul a decision is to reverse or cancel it

explanation.surface: A book's answer gets printed backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In reverse' suggests turning letters round, but 'reverse' is a verb meaning to cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book, often for children, published once each year.

clue.text: Boyfriend's spoken of Cockney area

indicators.note: spoken of means the word is said out loud

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London; a true Cockney is born within the sound of Bow bells

explanation.surface: A girl talks of her boyfriend from the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an admirer or sweetheart, a boyfriend.

clue.text: Bill the schoolmaster

definitions.meaning: British public-school slang for a teacher

explanation.definitionFit: A bird's mouthpart and old slang for a teacher or magistrate share this word.

clue.text: Desired win, fired missile

indicators.note: fired suggests the letters are let loose and reshaped

explanation.surface: Eager for victory, someone launches a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sidewinder is an air-to-air guided missile named after a rattlesnake.

clue.text: Yet later in the day

definitions.meaning: used to strengthen a comparison, as 'yet' or 'still'

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning still and the poetic noun for evening share this spelling.

clue.text: At home son meets pressure, causing rebellion

parts.note: in means at home
urgency means pressing need, pressure

explanation.surface: A son living at home is under pressure, so he rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgency is an armed uprising against authority.
